# 3 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Liberation, Celebration, and Return

---

**1** When the king had sent this letter to the generals in each of the cities with such instructions, he allowed the Jews to return to their homes.

**2** He gave orders that the soldiers scattered throughout the cities were to respect and honor the Jews.

**3** He also commanded that all the property of the Jews that had been confiscated should be restored to them intact, and that those who had been entrusted with any of their goods should return them immediately and without any deception.

**4** Furthermore, those who had committed offenses against the Jews were to be punished, and those who had spoken against them were to receive their due punishment.

**5** He urged his officials to treat all the Jews in their territory with every kindness and goodwill.

**6** After the king had issued this letter, the Jews gathered at a convenient place in great joy and began to celebrate with prayers and songs of praise.

**7** They established that day as a joyful festival, a day of great gladness, calling it a day of great salvation.

**8** The king also granted them a three-day celebration with a great feast, with singing and with toasting one another.

**9** And the Jews who had been taken away to various parts of Egypt returned home with joy and gladness.

**10** Delivered from death itself, they returned to their families and their homes.

**11** From that day forward they resolved to celebrate this day as a day of great joy throughout the time they dwelt in Egypt.

**12** They also sent letters to their brothers in Jerusalem, reporting all that had happened to them and calling the day a festival.

**13** And all rejoiced together in the great works that God had done for his people Israel, making it known that he is with them and cares for them.

**14** The delivered Jews gathered together and resolved to observe this festival in their community for all time, in whatever places they might live.

**15** They called it the Phruraia, the feast of salvation, a day of joy and gladness.

**16** And the glory of the God of Israel was made known throughout all the people.

**17** For the God of Israel is the God who does wonders among men, and he delivered his people from destruction.

**18** Blessed is the Lord who has saved Israel from all its distresses.

**19** And the people of Israel praised God with songs of thanksgiving and joyful praise.

**20** Great is the glory of the God of Israel, the God who alone does wondrous things among his people.
